title: Etale source-cover structural descent and geometric-fibre preparation
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $(h_i:U_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ be etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism] whose images cover $X$. Then $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] if and only if every $f\circ h_i$ is flat, and $f$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] if and only if every $f\circ h_i$ is locally of finite presentation. Assume either of the equivalent finite-presentation conditions. For every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and morphism $g:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], put $C=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $D_i=U_i\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. There are canonical isomorphisms $D_i\cong U_i\times_X C$ over $C$, characterized by their projections to $U_i$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Under these identifications the projections $e_i:D_i\to C$ are etale and jointly surjective. The schemes $C$ and all $D_i$ are locally of finite type over $\Omega$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. For any finite-presentation affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ above $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ through which $g$ factors, its pullback is $\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega\otimes_R A)$ and its algebra is finitely presented over $\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]; the same holds for each $U_i$. These charts cover the respective fibres. No quasi-compactness, separatedness or Noetherian assumption on $X,S,U_i$ is made. Empty sources, empty fibres and the empty covering of the empty source are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0C5D, lemma-nodal-family-etale-local-source, structural descent and geometric-fibre preparation (old steps 1--4); descent.tex Tags 036K lemma-flat-fpqc-local-source and 036N lemma-locally-finite-presentation-fppf-local-source; algebra.tex Tag 05G5 lemma-base-change-finiteness (4); morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 lemma-finite-type-noetherian

proof.text: Each $h_i$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose $f$ is flat. At $u\in U_i$, writing $x=h_i(u)$ and $s=f(x)$, the stalk map of $fh_i$ is the composite $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O_{U_i,u}$. Both maps are flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism], so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp] makes the composite flat. Thus every $fh_i$ is flat.

source.place: Tag 036K, lemma-flat-fpqc-local-source, forward implication on local rings

proof.text: Conversely suppose all $fh_i$ are flat. For any $x\in X$ choose $i,u$ with $h_i(u)=x$ and set $A=\mathcal O_{S,f(x)}$, $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $E=\mathcal O_{U_i,u}$. The map $B\to E$ is flat and local, hence faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat]. The composite $A\to E$ is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Apply [lem-trf-flatness-faithfully-flat-extension] to $A\to B\to E$ and $N=B$: multiplication identifies $E\otimes_B B$ with $E$, with inverse $e\mapsto e\otimes1$, and respects the $A$-actions. It follows that $B$ is flat over $A$. This holds at every $x$, proving flatness of $f$.

source.place: Tag 036K, lemma-flat-fpqc-local-source, reverse implication; algebra.tex Tag 0584, lemma-flatness-descends-more-general (2)

proof.text: The family $(h_i)$ is jointly surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, the latter two properties having been extracted from [def-weil-etale-morphism] in step 1. Apply [lem-trf-lfp-fppf-source-locality] to precisely this family. Its two implications prove the asserted equivalence for local finite presentation, without assuming that $f$ is flat. For the remaining steps assume these equivalent conditions, so both $f$ and every $fh_i$ are locally of finite presentation.

Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $a_i:D_i\to U_i\times_X C$ with components $p_{U_i}$ and $(h_i p_{U_i},p_T)$, and $b_i:U_i\times_X C\to D_i$ with components $q_{U_i}$ and $p_Tq_C$. The required compatibility equations are respectively the defining equations of $D_i$ and $U_i\times_X C$. Both composites have the same two projections as the corresponding identity, so uniqueness in that universal property proves $a_ib_i=1$ and $b_ia_i=1$. The map to $C$ is preserved and the projections to $U_i,T$ characterize this isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] to $(h_i)$ and $C\to X$. It gives an etale jointly surjective family $C\times_X U_i\to C$; exchanging the two factors, again by their projection universal property, gives $U_i\times_X C\to C$. Under $a_i$, these maps are exactly $e_i=(h_i p_{U_i},p_T)$.

source.place: Tag 0C5D, lemma-nodal-family-etale-local-source, taking fibres; morphisms.tex Tags 02GO/01S1 (base change of etale maps/surjectivity)

proof.text: Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ containing the image of $g$; it exists by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Since $T$ has one point, $g$ factors through $V$. Cover $f^{-1}(V)$ by affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ using the same basis lemma. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], $R\to A$ is finitely presented. The pullback $W\times_S T=W\times_V T$ is an open subscheme of $C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]; its image is the inverse image of $W$, since a map into an open subscheme is exactly a map whose image lies in that open. Thus these opens cover $C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] with the two factors ordered as $T,W$: it identifies this open with $\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega\otimes_R A)$, with the specified structure and projection maps. By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] this is a finitely presented $\Omega$-algebra. The same argument, now with $fh_i$ in place of $f$, gives such a covering of each $D_i$. It also proves the formula for every finite-presentation affine chart specified in the statement, not just the chosen covers.

source.place: Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes; Tag 01JY, lemma-base-change-immersion; morphisms.tex Tag 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize; algebra.tex Tag 05G5 (4), lemma-base-change-finiteness

proof.text: A finite presentation $\Omega[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m)$ is generated as an $\Omega$-algebra by the finitely many images of the $t_j$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. The affine covers in step 5 therefore show that $C$ and each $D_i$ are locally of finite type over $\Omega$ by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Indeed, the only nonempty open of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is itself. Every ideal of the field $\Omega$ is either zero or contains a unit and is the whole ring, generated respectively by $0$ or $1$. Thus $\Omega$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and its spectrum is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to the structure maps of $C$ and $D_i$ to obtain their local Noetherianity. If a source or fibre is empty, its pointwise conditions and affine-cover assertions are vacuous. The empty covering of empty $X$ causes no choice in step 2. All choices and arguments above are local; no finite subcover, separatedness, or condition on the base beyond those stated has been used.

lean.statement: theorem etale_source_fibre_preparation {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) {I : Type v} (U : I → Scheme.{u}) (h : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ X) [∀ i : I, Etale (h i)] (hjoint : ∀ x : X, ∃ (i : I) (y : U i), h i y = x) : (Flat f ↔ ∀ i : I, Flat (h i ≫ f)) ∧ (LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ↔ ∀ i : I, LocallyOfFinitePresentation (h i ≫ f)) ∧ (LocallyOfFinitePresentation f → ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (g : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S), (∀ i : I, ∃! a : pullback (h i ≫ f) g ≅ pullback (h i) (pullback.fst f g), a.hom ≫ pullback.fst (h i) (pullback.fst f g) = pullback.fst (h i ≫ f) g ∧ a.hom ≫ pullback.snd (h i) (pullback.fst f g) ≫ pullback.snd f g = pullback.snd (h i ≫ f) g) ∧ (∀ i : I, Etale ((pullbackRightPullbackFstIso f g (h i)).inv ≫ pullback.snd (h i) (pullback.fst f g))) ∧ (∀ x : (pullback f g : Scheme.{u}), ∃ (i : I) (y : (pullback (h i ≫ f) g : Scheme.{u})), ((pullbackRightPullbackFstIso f g (h i)).inv ≫ pullback.snd (h i) (pullback.fst f g)) y = x) ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType (pullback.snd f g) ∧ IsLocallyNoetherian (pullback f g) ∧ ∀ i : I, LocallyOfFiniteType (pullback.snd (h i ≫ f) g) ∧ IsLocallyNoetherian (pullback (h i ≫ f) g))
lean.note: All clauses are carried by the main theorem and the two recorded affine-chart theorems: geometric_fibre_finite_presentation_affine_chart and geometric_fibre_finite_presentation_affine_charts_cover. Canonical comparison uses Mathlib pullbackRightPullbackFstIso, not a new construction.
